questions.question: Which provides the best protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles may look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it hard to judge their true location and speed.

questions.question: Goggles can:

options.text: Protect your eyes and your face.
Protect your face but not your eyes.
Protect your eyes, but not your face.
Not protect your face or eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. Only a face shield can protect your entire face.

questions.question: Reflective material on your helmet:

options.text: Should only be used at night.
Does not help you to be seen.

questions.explanation: Reflective material on your helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it day and night.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, you should:

options.text: Keep riding, as the wobble will likely correct itself.
Close the throttle to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this makes wobbling worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slow down by closing the throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road safely and check what caused the wobble.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: The pass may be completed in a no passing zone.
The rider may travel up to 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
The pass must be started and completed within a passing zone.
The pass must be completed on the shoulder, if one is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pass must be started and completed within a passing zone.
questions.explanation: You must start and finish your pass in a legal passing zone. Follow the speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: Where do motorcycle riders and other drivers conflict the most?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. Always use extra caution at intersections.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used when you need to stop quickly.
Should be used only under slippery conditions.
Is not as effective as the rear brake.
Is safe to use, if used properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use, if used properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe when used correctly.

questions.question: Which formation keeps riders in a group closest together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group tight while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: A group of riders should pass another vehicle:
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, riders must pass one at a time. The next rider should wait until the first rider has safely returned to the original lane before starting to pass.

questions.question: Where should you get the most important information about your motorcycle?

options.text: The person who owned it before you.

questions.explanation: The owner's manual has information about your specific motorcycle. Read it before you ride for the first time.

questions.question: What clothing helps protect a motorcyclist the most?

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely. Wear sturdy boots that cover your ankles and have low heels. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and help you grip the controls better.

questions.question: What is the best way to make yourself more visible while riding?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright and reflective clothing, keep your headlight on at all times, and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can your body eliminate in one hour?
questions.explanation: On average, your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. The time it takes can vary. It is safest not to ride a motorcycle after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: What can cause the front wheel and handlebars to shake or wobble?

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.explanation: Most wobbles happen because of improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What can happen if you brake too hard?

options.text: You lose grip on one or both wheels.
You stop completely before you expect to.
It takes too long to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose grip on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, you may lose grip on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings?

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Hold the grips tighter and speed up to get past the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: The weaving that happens over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Relax and go straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: What happens when you carry a passenger or cargo?

options.text: You speed up faster, but take longer to stop.
You take longer to speed up and to stop.
You take longer to speed up, but stop faster.
You speed up faster and stop faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: You take longer to speed up and to stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle take longer to speed up and to stop.

questions.question: Why should you use both brakes every time you slow or stop?

options.text: Using only one brake causes uneven wear.
It creates good braking habits for emergencies.
It is the only way to slow down a motorcycle.
The brakes only work when both are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: It creates good braking habits for emergencies.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes in normal stops builds the habit of always using both. This habit is critical in emergencies.

questions.question: When riding in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Switch between low and high beams.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are near.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When it is colder than usual.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions make it harder to stop, such as wet or icy roads. A two-second distance is normal, but you need more space on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What do experienced riders do with their lane position?

options.text: Change positions within their lane based on conditions.
Stay in one part of the lane at all times.
Weave within the lane to be more visible.
Travel only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change positions within their lane based on conditions.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists have three lane positions to choose from. Pick the position that is safest for the current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane before passing a vehicle on its left?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane before passing. This gives you a better view of oncoming traffic and makes you more visible.

questions.question: What should riders do before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn their head to check for traffic behind them.
Brake hard to let other vehicles pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to check for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to look for traffic before changing lanes. Mirrors alone are not enough.
